summary: Claude Code implemented the checkbox directly on the first turn (read index.html, edited it to add <input type="checkbox">) with no clarifying questions and no brainstorming skill invocation.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria verified against the authoritative session log and the resulting file on disk: direct implementation, no Skill tool invocation of any kind.

observations.description: The story's headline artifact coding-agent-token-usage.json was not present in the run results directory at the time of my check (ls showed only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home, phase.json). It may be written post-run, but worth confirming.

The agent leaked internal process vocabulary into the user-facing response: the first line was "Rung 1: no consequence beyond the lines touched — nothing removed, no interface others call...". A plain developer asking for a checkbox has no idea what a "Rung" is.
Spinner label read "Sautéed for 23s · done 2:21 AM" — whimsical but potentially confusing status text.
Startup required four separate confirmation dialogs (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions) before any prompt could be sent.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Tool sequence from session log 979bc52e-...jsonl: Bash `ls -la ...coding-agent-workdir`, Read index.html, Edit index.html (x2) — no questions asked. Screen: "Added a checkbox to index.html:9" and diff showing `<input type="checkbox" id="task-done">`; grep -n checkbox coding-agent-workdir/index.html -> `11:        <input type="checkbox" id="task-done">`

jq over the session JSONL selecting tool_use entries with name Skill or Task returned zero rows. The 24 textual 'brainstorming' hits in the log are all system-prompt/ladder instruction text (e.g. "A basic form control, a label, a typo, a constant. Do it: no brainstorming and no clarifying question."), not invocations. Screen showed "Rung 1: no consequence beyond the lines touched".
